tagline: A gravel road between the Mid Hills pinyons and Hole-in-the-Wall.
intro: Wild Horse Canyon Road leaves Black Canyon Road at the Mid Hills and rejoins it just south of Hole-in-the-Wall, a gravel byway through the middle of Mojave National Preserve. On the way it passes near Wild Horse Mesa.

There is a walkers' version as well. An eight-mile trail runs between the same two ends, through a maze of washes decorated with barrel and cholla cacti, then through the ground burned in the Hackberry Fire, with 1,200 feet of climbing in all.

moments.title: Mid Hills
moments.text: About two miles in from Black Canyon Road, the campground sits in pinyon and juniper woodland. The 2005 Hackberry Fire still shows, though the back half keeps its shade.

moments.title: Hole-in-the-Wall
moments.text: Just north of the road's south end, rhyolite cliffs riddled with holes and hollows make the backdrop, and the Rings Trail threads Banshee Canyon from the visitor center.

practical: Mid Hills Campground is not recommended for RVs. Off the pavement there are no services, and UTVs and ATVs are prohibited on all preserve roads.
